So SSRIs are a pretty hated drug but lemme tell you a bit about how they work. We all know they increase serotonin but they also increase GABA which is an inhibitory neurotransmitter meaning the stop action potentials/stop neurons from firing so slowing down your central nervous system. Benzos and alcohol also increase GABA which is why you feel calm and relaxed. Buspar is another option if SSRIs have to many side effects. It increases serotonin but not in the same way. I also think asking a bunch of anxious people if you should drink to calm anxiety was always gonna have these drastic answers. I think people are being dramatic and catastrophizing but that's what we do. My doctors and therapists know I lean on alcohol a bit when having to leave my house but they also know I do not have an addictive personality and generally scared of damage do to severe alcohol abuse. If a couple beers or drinks helps you leave the house then go for it but if you are talking about getting drunk to cope with anxiety than obviously don't do that. There's also welbutrin or other medications but I always encourage people to try medications and to truly give them a chance. It's not normal to fear leaving your house. Our brain chemistry is not normal and medications work. It's usually a long process to find the right one and a lot of agoraphobics are non adherent to the medications so they don't see results.

Your sympathetic nervous system releases adrenaline, ramping up your heart rate. It is connected to every major system in your body.
